subject: Re: Redwood model fit & benchmarks — FinPay next steps
messages:

Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood — follow-up & next steps from today

Hi Samira — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and suggested next steps: 

- Primary goal: augment FinPay's customer support triage with an LLM-powered intent classifier + concise automated replies, while keeping latency under 150ms p95 for UI flows.
- Main constraints: PII-sanitization pipeline, on-prem deployment option for EU customers (later phase), and strict SLA expectations for peak traffic (TPS bursts ~200).

What we discussed as immediate next steps:
1) I'll share our recommended model variants and Redwood-verified benchmark links (latency percentiles, TPS tests) so your infra team can validate.
2) If the benchmarks look reasonable, we can run a short eval using your prompt set to validate quality/regression risk.
3) Marissa will share a deck + the benchmark CSV and recommended prompt set example.

Marissa — looping you in to drop the benchmark links and the prompt set we discussed. Samira / Mike — feel free to flag any follow-up questions.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez

From: Samira Khan <samira@finpay.com>

Date: 2026-10-29T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — follow-up & next steps from today

Appreciate the recap, Alex. A few clarifying Qs before we kick off the eval: 

- For latency targets: the 150ms p95 you mentioned — is that for a single-token step or end-to-end generation for short replies (~20 tokens)? We typically measure end-to-end in our UI.
- On TPS: our spike profile is ~200 TPS for classification traffic, but reply generation is lower (20–30 TPS). Would you recommend different model variants for classify vs. generate?

Also, we need the benchmark artifacts and a quick read on likely quality regressions for model variants. Mike and I will share a sanitized sample prompt set tonight.

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Customer Ops, FinPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finpay.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — benchmark links & recommended variants for FinPay

Hi Samira — attaching the artifacts we discussed and a short note on recommendations. See Drive + quick summary below.

Attachments: finpay_benchmark_results.csv, redwood_performance_profiles.pdf, finpay_prompt_set_v1.json

Summary (high level):
- Recommended variants:
  • redwood-llama-13b-v2-quant (classification): best latency/TPS tradeoff for classification. In our tests it sustained 220 TPS at ~60ms mean latency on a 2xA100 pool.
  • redwood-llama-13b-v2-quant-gen (generation): same family but tuned for response quality; p95 latency ~140ms for ~20-token replies on an n1-standard equivalent baseline (see linked profile).
  • redwood-open-7b (low-cost baseline): suitable for non-critical flows where quality can be slightly lower; p95 ~220ms under similar test conditions.

- Redwood-verified performance profiles (in PDF): include detailed TPS curves, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), hardware config used, and test prompts (short reply / classification). Link: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/finpay-2026-10-30

- Quality/regression risks: we ran the FinPay sample prompt set and flagged 12 prompts with potential hallucination / entity-misassignment on the open-7b baseline. The 13b family showed substantially fewer failures but higher cost. We recommend running a focused eval on your sanitized prompt set to measure intent precision/recall and generation ROUGE/semantic metrics.

- Next steps we propose:
  1) You upload the sanitized prompt set (or confirm the attached v1 is OK).
  2) We run a short eval (2–4k prompt pairs) on redwood-llama-13b-v2-quant and redwood-open-7b and return a quality+perf matrix.
  3) If results look good, we can provision a short dedicated test pool for FinPay to smoke test under your traffic profile.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/finpay-prompt-sets, https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/FIN-2026-089

Let us know which prompts to prioritize and any additional constraints (PII masking, tokenization concerns).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_performance_profiles.pdf]

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@finpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — benchmark links & recommended variants for FinPay

Thanks Marissa — and thanks Samira for the quick replies. Quick confirmations and plan: 

- Samira: measuring end-to-end UI latency for ~20-token replies is exactly how we captured the p95 numbers in the attached profile. So the ~140ms p95 for the 13b-gen variant maps to your metric. Classification numbers are measured as per-request inference latency for single-label classification (that’s where the 60ms mean / 220 TPS numbers come from).
- We recommend starting with a two-arm eval: redwood-llama-13b-v2-quant (classification + gen variant) vs redwood-open-7b (baseline) so you can compare quality and cost.

Action items:
1) Samira / Mike: confirm you uploaded the sanitized prompt set (or confirm the attached finpay_prompt_set_v1.json is cleared to use).
2) Marissa / Dylan: run the 2–4k eval on both variants and produce the quality + perf matrix (please include p50/p90/p95/p99 and TPS curves).
3) Alex: schedule a 30-min results review next week once we have the eval output (I’ll send a calendar invite after Samira confirms).

Calendar proposal: Tue 2026-11-09 10:00 AM PT — I’ll send invite if that works for you.

If there are any compliance-required evidence items we should surface before the eval (SOC2 scope or data handling), flag them here and we’ll loop in Security.

Best,
Alex Martinez
